documents.title: Office Visit — asthma, spring allergies
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spring asthma/allergy check.

Asthma: no night symptoms, no limitation, albuterol used twice since the fall. Fluticasone 44 2 puffs BID. ACT above 20.
Nose: pollen season started, sneezing and itchy eyes, OTC antihistamine helping.
Skin: the sun reaction from October cleared completely, no scarring. Acne is about where it was, she's not asking for anything for it right now.
Off HCTZ since October; no swelling, no headaches outside her usual migraine pattern.
Mood: anxiety manageable, sertraline 100 via psychiatry.

Meds: fluticasone HFA 44 2 puffs BID; albuterol PRN; sertraline 100 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal tree and grass pollens.

BP 114/76, HR 74, RR 14, T 36.8, SpO2 98%. Wt 66.0 kg.
Nasal mucosa a little swollen, clear drainage. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Skin of face and forearms normal; mild comedonal acne chin.

A/P
1. Mild persistent asthma — well controlled, continue.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis — in season, OTC antihistamine.
3. BP normal off HCTZ.
4. Acne vulgaris — no treatment for now.
Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Office Visit — swelling, rash, joint pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, achy, legs swelling, rash on face. About 3 weeks.

HPI: 33 y/o F. Three weeks of fatigue, aching joints and swelling of both legs. New red rash across both cheeks, flares when she's in the sun. No fever, no recent infection, no travel. No new medicines; over the counter, only her usual antihistamine in pollen season and a cough syrup now and then. Off HCTZ since the photosensitivity in October. Mother has SLE.

Meds: fluticasone HFA 44 2 puffs BID; albuterol PRN; sertraline 100 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal tree and grass pollens.

Exam: BP 151/92, HR 78, RR 16, T 37.0, SpO2 98%. Wt 66.7 kg.
Tired-appearing, not ill. Erythematous rash over both malar areas. Pitting edema both lower legs up to the shins. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur, no rub. Abdomen soft, nontender. Joints: no visible swelling.

Office urine dipstick: protein and blood positive. Sent for microscopy.

A/P
New edema, BP well above her usual, protein and blood in the urine, malar rash and joint pain in a woman whose mother has SLE. This needs nephrology now, not a routine referral.
- Called nephrology on call this morning. They will see her Monday 6/30 and expect to admit for workup.
- Urgent referral sent with today's note; UA to follow.
- Avoid NSAIDs. Low salt. Elevate legs.
- If short of breath, chest pain, much less urine, or worse swelling over the weekend: ED.
She's scared; spent time with her. Her partner is driving her Monday.

documents.title: Urinalysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: UA back: protein and blood positive, microscopy with many RBCs and red cell casts. Faxed to nephrology ahead of Monday. Pt aware.

events.reason: Proteinuria and hematuria with red cell casts, edema, malar rash

medications.sig: 500 mg IV once daily for 3 days (6/30-7/2/2025)

reports.text: Specimen: kidney, left, percutaneous needle core biopsy under ultrasound guidance (both kidneys normal in size on the guiding ultrasound). Adequacy: adequate; cortex present with sufficient glomeruli for evaluation. Light microscopy, immunofluorescence and electron microscopy reviewed together. Glomeruli show active lesions. No significant glomerulosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis or tubular atrophy.
reports.conclusion: Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class IV, with active lesions and no significant chronic damage.

documents.title: Nephrology admission H&P
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — NEPHROLOGY ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Admitted: 06/30/2025
Referring: primary care (urgent)

Chief complaint: three weeks of fatigue, joint pain and leg swelling, with a new facial rash.

HPI: 33 year old woman with prior hydrochlorothiazide-induced photosensitivity (October 2024). For three weeks she has felt run down, with aching joints and swollen legs. She has also developed a red rash across both cheeks that gets worse with sun. No recent infections. No travel. Her PCP found blood, protein and casts in the urine last week and called us.

PMH: mild persistent asthma; seasonal allergic rhinitis; OCD; generalized anxiety disorder; migraine without aura; acne vulgaris. Hydrochlorothiazide photosensitivity 10/2024.
PSH: none.

Home medications:
- albuterol HFA 90 mcg: 1-2 puffs q4-6h PRN
- fluticasone propionate HFA 44 mcg, 2 puffs twice daily
- sertraline 100 mg daily
- sumatriptan 50 mg as needed (max 200 mg/day)
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily: STOPPED 10/2024 (photosensitivity)
She uses her albuterol inhaler only occasionally.

Allergies: seasonal pollens (tree, grass); hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity).

Family history: mother with SLE; father with asthma and seasonal allergies; sister with major depressive disorder.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks per month; graphic designer.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 86, RR 16, T 36.8, SpO2 98% RA.
General: fatigued, no distress. Skin: erythematous malar rash. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no rub, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities: bilateral pitting edema to the shins. Joints: no synovitis.

Labs (6/30): urinalysis with protein and blood, red blood cell casts on microscopy. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL. Albumin 2.8 g/dL. 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g. ANA positive.

Assessment: active urine sediment with heavy proteinuria, low albumin, edema and raised blood pressure, together with a photosensitive malar rash and arthralgia. Strong concern for lupus nephritis.

Plan: complement levels and anti-dsDNA sent. Kidney biopsy 7/1. Given the proteinuria and active sediment, IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily x 3 days started 6/30 after discussion with the patient. Daily weights, low salt diet.

ADDENDUM 07/01/2025 08:40: C3 low. C4 low. Anti-dsDNA positive. With the positive ANA, this is systemic lupus erythematosus presenting with a lupus nephritis flare. Rheumatology aware. Biopsy proceeding today.

Nephrology

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 06/30/2025   Discharged: 07/03/2025
Service: Nephrology

Principal diagnosis: systemic lupus erythematosus presenting with lupus nephritis flare, ISN/RPS class IV.

Hospital course:
Admitted from clinic with protein, blood and red cell casts in the urine, 24-hour protein 4.5 g, creatinine 1.2, albumin 2.8, BP 145/90, leg edema and a photosensitive malar rash. ANA and anti-dsDNA positive, C3 and C4 low.
Received IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for 3 days (6/30 to 7/2).
Ultrasound-guided left kidney biopsy 7/1, uncomplicated: class IV lupus nephritis with active lesions, no significant chronic damage.
BP improving at discharge (132/84 this morning). Edema slowly improving.

Discharge medications:
NEW
- prednisone 40 mg by mouth daily
- mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg by mouth twice daily
- hydroxychloroquine 200 mg by mouth daily
- losartan 25 mg by mouth daily (proteinuria and blood pressure)
CONTINUE
- albuterol HFA as needed; fluticasone HFA 44 mcg 2 puffs twice daily; sertraline 100 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg as needed
Allergies: seasonal pollens; hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity).

Counselling: mycophenolate and losartan can harm a pregnancy and must not be taken if pregnant; she reports reliable contraception. Sun protection. Infection precautions on immunosuppression.

Follow-up:
- Outside nephrology clinic in 2 to 3 months, labs before.
- Outside rheumatology new-patient visit, being scheduled.
- PCP within 1 week.

Nephrology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admitted 6/30-7/3: new SLE presenting as lupus nephritis, biopsy class IV, active, no chronic damage. Pulse methylpred x3, then discharged on prednisone 40, MMF 1000 BID, HCQ 200, losartan 25.

Today: energy slowly coming back. Legs less swollen each day. Rash on cheeks fading. Joints achy in the mornings but better. Prednisone keeping her up at night, appetite up. Taking every medicine as listed; MMF PA approved and filled. Biopsy site fine.
Reports reliable contraception, understands MMF and losartan are not safe in pregnancy.

Meds reconciled (discharge list = what she's taking): prednisone 40 mg daily, mycophenolate 1000 mg BID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, losartan 25 mg daily, fluticasone HFA 44 2 puffs BID, albuterol PRN, sertraline 100 mg daily, sumatriptan 50 mg PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal tree and grass pollens.

BP 128/82, HR 84, RR 14, T 36.8, SpO2 98%. Wt 67.1 kg.
Faint malar erythema. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no rub. Abdomen soft. Pitting edema at the ankles, less than at the 6/27 visit. Left flank biopsy site clean.

A/P
1. SLE with lupus nephritis, class IV — improving on induction. Same regimen. CMP and CBC today. Nephrology follow-up in September; rheumatology new-patient visit being scheduled for August (she'll call me if no date by next week).
2. Hydroxychloroquine — baseline eye exam needed; referral placed.
3. Immunosuppressed: PCV20 today. No live vaccines. Flu and shingles vaccine in the fall. Sun protection.
4. Asthma, anxiety, migraine — unchanged. Sumatriptan OK as before.
5. Work note given (flexible/remote hours for the next 6 weeks).
TCM: discharge 7/3, interactive contact 7/7, face-to-face 7/10.
RTC ~3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/12/2025
Referred from: inpatient nephrology / primary care

Ms. Williams is a 33 year old woman hospitalized 6/30 to 7/3/2025 with a lupus nephritis flare as the presenting manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus. Kidney biopsy showed ISN/RPS class IV with active lesions and no significant chronic damage. She received three days of IV methylprednisolone and was discharged on prednisone 40 mg daily, mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and losartan 25 mg daily.

She describes the photosensitive rash across the cheeks and aching joints that came on in the weeks before admission, both now easing. Swelling in the legs is better. She is tolerating the mycophenolate. Mother has SLE.

Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal pollens.

Exam: BP 123/74, HR 80, weight 66.6 kg. Faint residual malar erythema. Mouth without ulcers. Joints without synovitis today. Heart and lungs normal.

Assessment: Systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis (class IV), malar rash and arthralgia, responding to induction.

Plan:
1. Continue mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and losartan 25 mg daily.
2. Begin prednisone taper today; written schedule given to the patient. Nephrology is aware.
3. Baseline hydroxychloroquine eye exam (referral already placed by her PCP).
4. Strict sun protection.
5. Return in about 5 months, sooner for a flare.

Rheumatology

documents.title: RE: Pottery studio?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, please go. Wash your hands when you arrive and before you eat, skip it on days someone there is obviously sick, and keep wearing sunscreen if you walk there. Call if you get a fever, since on mycophenolate we want to hear about it early.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
YEARLY PHYSICAL + LUPUS FOLLOW-UP
34 y/o F.

Lupus: seen by rheumatology 8/12 (taper started), eye exam 9/9 normal, nephrology 9/23 (creatinine 1.0, albumin 3.3, UPCR 2.2, C3 still low, C4 normal). Feels much more like herself. Leg swelling gone for a few weeks now. Cheek rash has cleared. Joints only stiff now and then. Taking MMF, HCQ, losartan and the prednisone taper exactly as written.
Asthma: quiet. Albuterol not needed since spring. ACT above 20.
Migraine: one or two a month, sumatriptan works.
Mood: anxious about the lupus at times but coping; back at the pottery studio. PHQ-9 = 3.

Meds: mycophenolate 1000 mg BID; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; losartan 25 mg daily; prednisone taper per rheumatology; fluticasone HFA 44 2 puffs BID; albuterol PRN; sertraline 100 mg daily; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (photosensitivity); seasonal tree and grass pollens.

BP 122/78, HR 76, RR 14, T 36.7, SpO2 99%. Wt 66.7 kg.
Well. No malar rash. Mouth clear. Neck: no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no rub or murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Joints: no swelling or tenderness. Legs: no edema. Skin: mild acne chin.

A/P
1. SLE with lupus nephritis — clinically improving; edema resolved, rash cleared. BP in good range on losartan. CBC and BMP today. Continue regimen per specialists.
2. Health maintenance (immunosuppressed): flu vaccine, Shingrix dose 1 and 2025-26 COVID vaccine today. Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months. PCV20 done 7/2025. No live vaccines. Now that she is immunosuppressed, will repeat the cervical co-test in early 2026 rather than waiting until 2028. Lipids deferred while the proteinuria settles.
3. Mild persistent asthma — well controlled.
4. Migraine without aura — stable.
5. GAD/OCD — psychiatry, sertraline 100.
6. Acne, allergic rhinitis — no change.
RTC 3-4 months.
